transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-04 11:00 UTC
Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Liam Carter (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Dr. Emily Chen (Silverpine CTO), Raj Patel (Silverpine VP Eng), Sofia Gomez (Silverpine Head of MLOps)

Summary: quick walkthrough of Redwood model catalog and guidance on selecting open models for Silverpine's triage assistant. Demo focused on benchmark results, compatibility matrix (quantization, GPU families), and deployment modes with security requirements. Next steps: share benchmarks, schedule SE deep dive, customer to provide prompt set for pilot.

Transcript:
[00:00] Liam: All right, thanks everyone for joining, really appreciate you carving time. I'm Liam from Redwood, AE on this account. With me is Maya Singh, our SE who will walk through the model catalog and the benchmark stuff.
[00:12] Maya: hey hi all, I'll share my screen in a sec, can everyone see?
[00:16] Emily: yep we can see it, looks good.
[00:20] Liam: quick agenda, demo the model catalog UI, talk through recommended open models for clinical triage, show benchmark numbers (latency/throughput/cost), then compatibility matrix - which models we recommend on A100 vs H100 vs T4 and quantization notes, and finally Q&A on security and next steps.
[00:33] Raj: great, timeline wise we have a Q2 pilot budget, hope to pick a model and run a pilot in March.
[00:39] Maya: perfect, we'll aim to make that easy. jumping into the model catalog - so this is Redwood Console > Model Catalog. On the left you can filter by task (chat, generation, embeddings), license (MIT, Apache), and by performance profile.
[00:52] Maya: for clinical triage we typically look at models with strong instruction following and hallucination behavior - we've curated a shortlist here: open-llama-3-13b, medformer-11b (community fine-tuned), and redwood-verified-flan-xxl (open variant).
[01:12] Emily: when you say redwood-verified-flan, is that a fine-tuned checkpoint you provide or an upstream model you point to?
[01:18] Maya: it's an upstream open variant that we run through our verification harness - we produce performance profiles and a reproducible benchmark. we don't change the weights unless you opt for a managed fine-tune or RLHF service.
[01:29] Raj: can you show the benchmark numbers? we care about 95p latency under 2s for single-turn triage prompts and throughput for batch processing.
[01:36] Maya: yes, here's a benchmark sheet - link: drive/benchmarks/silverpine-models (shared). the console shows median/95p latency, tokens/s, and cost-per-1k-tokens using our hosted pricing and also estimates for Dedicated on A100/H100.
[01:50] Maya: for example, open-llama-3-13b at 512 tokens on H100 (fp16) runs ~420ms median, 95p around 1.1s; on A100 it's slightly higher. medformer-11b (quantized int4) gives ~320ms median but sacrifices a bit on safety/hallucination, so tradeoff there.
[02:10] Emily: medformer was community finetuned - curious about hallucination risk, do you have evals?
[02:15] Maya: yep we run our eval suite - quality monitors tied to prompt sets. we surfaced a 3-4% regression in factuality for medformer on our clinical prompts compared to redwood-verified-flan; we can share the eval export.
[02:27] Raj: on the Dedicated side, what's the unit economics look like? our infra team wants predictable throughput overnight for batch jobs.
[02:33] Liam: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools - you get predictable throughput and can set autoscale/burst policies. pricing is commit-based; I'll send a sample quote but rough math in console gives cost per 1M tokens and shows how batching and KV prefix caching reduce effective cost.
[02:47] Sofia: how does KV cache work with streaming? we need low-latency interactive triage and long histories for patients.
[02:53] Maya: our runtime supports continuous KV caching - it persists per-session KV and reuses cached prefixes when the prompt overlaps. streaming works with KV - but be careful, very long histories can increase 95p latency; we recommend summarization/condensed history and selective cache hits.
[03:12] Emily: we have strong security requirements - SOC2, SSO/SAML, KMS, and audit logs. can you confirm Redwood Private meets these and how audit logs are exposed?
[03:22] Liam: yes - Private includes a customer-controlled control plane and can be deployed VPC or on-prem. we integrate with cloud KMS providers and HSMs for key management and provide structured audit logs to your SIEM. we'll send the SOC2 and compliance pack.
[03:38] Raj: any gotchas around data residency? some of our clinics are in the EU, we need logs and data never leaving region.
[03:44] Maya: you can pin region for Dedicated and Private; hosted can be region-restricted but the dedicated/private options are safest for data residency. we'll include deployment options in the doc.
[03:57] Speaker 1: (inaudible)
[03:59] Maya: moving on to compatibility matrix - this is important: some models are quantization-friendly (LLM-quant support), others need H100 kernels for best perf. The Console shows a matrix: model vs GPU family vs supported quant modes (fp16, int8, int4) and recommended batch sizes.
[04:17] Maya: quick example: redwood-verified-flan-xxl on H100 fp16 gives best quality/latency combo, on A100 fp16 it's still good. open-llama-3-13b is very compatible with int8 and gives cost savings with minor throughput improvements. medformer-11b was trained with int4 in mind so it's cheap but quality delta shows in evals.
[04:35] Raj: do you support custom kernels or do we need to recompile? our infra team uses a custom kernel stack.
[04:40] Maya: the runtime chooses optimized kernels automatically; for very custom stacks we support on-prem packaging and can work with your infra team to validate kernels. some customers bring custom ops and we test them in our onboarding.
[04:52] Emily: does Redwood Optimize give recommendations about batching/quantization automatically?
[04:57] Maya: yes - Redwood Optimize analyzes your traffic patterns from traces and suggests batching, cache TTLs, and quantization profiles. it also simulates cost with different models and settings so you can pick a target latency or cost target and see tradeoffs.
[05:12] Liam: could be useful - we can run Optimize for a week on a sample workload and return recommended profiles.
[05:18] Raj: timeline - if we pick a model this month, how long to run a pilot?
[05:22] Maya: typical pilot: 2-3 weeks for smoke tests and quality evals, then a 4-6 week pilot for production-like load with dedicated capacity. varies if you want Private on-prem.
[05:33] Sofia: about SSO - SAML is required, role-based access control, and we need audit log retention for 2 years. is that supported out of the box?
[05:41] Liam: yes SAML SSO and RBAC supported; audit log retention is configurable for Dedicated/Private (hosted has standard retention tiers). we'll include retention options in the security pack.
[05:55] Emily: any concerns around model licensing? we need to ensure any model we pick can be used in a regulated clinical app.
[06:02] Maya: Console surfaces license info (MIT, Apache, custom) and flags models with restrictions. we also include provenance information. for clinical apps many customers choose Apache/MIT licensed models or sign a separate legal addendum for managed variants.
[06:16] Raj: what about monitoring/regression alerts when a model upgrade happens? we need to be able to detect quality regressions post-rollout.
[06:23] Maya: Redwood has quality monitoring connected to eval prompt sets. you can tag canary rollouts and run golden prompt sets, configure alert thresholds, and auto-roll back to a previous model if regressions exceed thresholds.
[06:35] Liam: any immediate blockers from your side for starting a pilot?
[06:39] Emily: security review is the main blocker - we need SOC2 docs, KMS integration details, and a data flow diagram.
[06:45] Sofia: plus we'd like to run a small benchmark on our prompts to verify latency numbers; can you replicate our environment?
[06:50] Maya: yes we can run benchmark reproductions - share a redacted prompt set and target token lengths and we'll run hosted and Dedicated estimates.
[06:58] Raj: one more - are there prebuilt safety/guardrails for PHI? we want deterministic redaction before passing to model ideally.
[07:04] Maya: we have an optional pre-processing chain and safety plugins; for PHI we recommend deterministic redaction at ingestion combined with post-generation filters. we can run that as part of pilot.
[07:16] Speaker 2 (customer): mm-hm
[07:18] Maya: switching back to the catalog UI - you can click "Compare" on two models to see side-by-side benchmarks, license, tokenization differences, and a compatibility matrix showing recommended hardware and quantization.
[07:30] Maya: also note our streaming vs batch latency visualization - it predicts 95p tail latencies under a given arrival distribution. it's not perfect but good for capacity planning.
[07:41] Emily: can you show a real example compare?
[07:44] Maya: sure - comparing open-llama-3-13b vs redwood-verified-flan-xxl (simulated using your prompt set). open-llama is cheaper and faster at lower context windows; flan-xxl has better factuality. here's the chart - you see cost-per-1M tokens and 95p latency side-by-side.
[07:58] Raj: are these numbers from your public benchmarks or run in our region?
[08:02] Maya: these are Redwood-verification runs in our public benchmark farm. for precise numbers we reproduce in your region or Dedicated cluster.
[08:13] Liam: we'll attach the raw benchmark spreadsheet so your infra can validate.
[08:18] Sofia: last question on compatibility matrix - do you include accelerator families like Apple M-? we have some edge inference plans.
[08:25] Maya: currently we profile NVIDIA families (T4, A100, H100) and some AMD/Arm setups; edge Apple M is not first-class but we can explore if you have a clear use case.
[08:40] Emily: ok makes sense.
[08:42] Maya: circling back to technical deep dive - is next week 3/11 for a longer SE-led session to run a sample benchmark with your prompts?
[08:50] Raj: 3/11 works for our SE folks.
[08:52] Liam: great I'll put a calendar invite.
[08:55] Emily: for the legal/procurement track, we need a sample contract and pricing to start internal approvals.
[09:01] Liam: I'll share a pricing outline for Hosted vs Dedicated and an MSA template.
[09:06] Maya: ok wrapping up, quick recap of recommended models: 1) redwood-verified-flan-xxl for highest quality and balanced latency on H100; 2) open-llama-3-13b if you need lower cost/latency at moderate quality; 3) medformer-11b (quantized) for aggressive cost targets but requires careful eval on hallucination.
[09:25] Emily: sounds good. we'll especially want the eval exports so our clinicians can review hallucination patterns.
[09:31] Maya: sure we'll include eval exports and prompts.
[09:34] Raj: action items?
[09:36] Liam: Maya to share benchmark spreadsheet and run notes, Liam to send pricing and contract outline, Sofia to provide sample prompts and redaction guidance, schedule SE deep dive 3/11.
[09:47] Sofia: noted, will send prompts by 3/8.
[09:50] Emily: thanks everyone, that was helpful.
[09:53] Liam: thank you, we'll follow up with the pack and invite.
[09:57] End of meeting.

References/shared artifacts: drive/benchmarks/silverpine-models (spreadsheet), https://redwood.ai/docs/model-catalog (console docs), security-pack/Silverpine (to be shared).

Notes on transcript quality: some microphone drops and small transcription errors (Speaker 1/2 labels appear briefly and one inaudible segment).
